- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.4) and price is trending up, model often overreacts; cap forecast increase at +1.5% above recent peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is consolidating, model often fails to mean-revert; apply slight downward bias (–0.5% to –1.5%) to avoid overconfidence.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window; apply 0.5–1.5% downward correction for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is high and price is near 30-day moving average, model often overestimates; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with sentiment-driven mean reversion.
